idiom_name: Watermill PoisonQueue middleware publishing unprocessable messages to a poison topic
implementation_notes: Watermill ships the pattern as middleware: PoisonQueue(pub, topic) returns a HandlerMiddleware that salvages unprocessable messages and publishes them on a separate topic while the main chain continues, and PoisonQueueWithFilter takes a predicate so only deterministic failures qualify. Go's explicit error returns replace the classic 'receiver inspects and routes' structure - the handler returns an error and the middleware owns the routing - and the same behaviour without Watermill is a small wrapper around any client library. Use the filtered variant whenever handler errors can be transient, otherwise every broker hiccup will fill the poison topic.
pitfalls: If the poison topic is subscribed by a handler that carries the same middleware, an unprocessable message circulates through the poison queue forever.
Without the filter every error - including transient publish failures - lands in the poison topic and buries the genuinely invalid messages.
The diverted copy must keep the original metadata (UUID, correlation id); dropping it leaves the error handler unable to correlate the frame with the sending system.
